caption:
is it purging or a breakout?
Only products that speed up skin turnover can purge you - and three checks tell most cases apart.

"Purging" is the flare some people get in the first weeks of a retinoid or an exfoliating acid. Spots that were already forming come up sooner. It is real enough to be on a drug label: the US label for one tretinoin gel lists an apparent worsening of inflammatory acne in the early weeks, and says more than seven weeks of use may be needed for sustained benefit.

Three checks:

The product. Does it contain a retinoid or an exfoliating acid? A plain moisturizer, cleanser or sunscreen has nothing in it to purge you.

The place. Purging shows up where you usually break out. New areas point somewhere else.

The clock. Purging usually settles within about 4-6 weeks. Still going past 8 is worth a second look.

When it is probably not purging: spots in new places, burning, itching or swelling, or deep painful lumps. Those are worth showing a doctor rather than pushing through.

What this does not mean: "purging" is a practical label, not a well-studied diagnosis. The 4-6 week window comes from clinical experience, not trials, and irritation can look the same.
